businessCase.splitNarrative: Roughly two thirds of the opportunity sits in aftersales — workshop throughput, parts availability and warranty recovery — with the remainder in the sales journey and shared integration estate.

talkTrack.constellation: MB Retail's operating fabric: 50 applications across 11 business portfolios and two customer journeys — Sales and Customer Service — serving dealerships across three markets.
talkTrack.serviceOps: Aftersales carries the incident load. Workshop and Parts together generate the majority of volume, and a single dealer-master sync failure fans out into hundreds of child alerts within minutes.
talkTrack.engOps: Change risk concentrates on the shared estate. Four systems are used by three or more portfolios, so a routine deploy can put the sales journey and the workshop at risk in the same window.
talkTrack.businessOps: Handover is the exposure. Every application it depends on is shared with an upstream portfolio, which means it has no independent failure domain of its own.
talkTrack.architecture: The estate grew by acquisition. DCP, VLMS and Xentry each appear in three portfolios, integration runs on a mix of MuleSoft and IBM MQ, and Oracle and SQL Server both carry master data.
talkTrack.finops: Spend is concentrated in the ERP and diagnostic layers, with a long tail of portfolio-specific tooling that never reaches scale.
talkTrack.securityOps: Identity sprawl across dealer-facing systems is the standing finding; third-party workshop tooling is the least governed surface.
talkTrack.agents: The ITIL run fleet handles detection through closure. Recovery and runbook selection stay in suggest mode pending sign-off; storm detection and severity classification already run live.
talkTrack.valuePool: The value case is built bottom-up from the workshop and parts bottlenecks rather than from a top-down cost baseline.
